name: Technology certification
description: Prepare for a vendor or industry certification (cloud, security, networking, data, project management...). Map the exam objectives, learn each domain with hands-on labs and finish with timed practice exams.

steps.title: Read the exam guide and map the objectives
steps.description: Download the official exam guide. List every domain with its weighting and turn each objective into a checkbox you can tick.

steps.title: Choose resources and book the exam
steps.description: Pick one main course, one source of practice questions and the official documentation. Book the exam date: a deadline makes the plan real.

steps.title: Set up a hands-on lab
steps.description: Create a free account or a local sandbox where you can build, break and rebuild things safely.

steps.title: Domain 1: the most heavily weighted
steps.description: Study the concepts, then do a lab for every objective. Write a short summary in your own words.

steps.title: Domain 2
steps.description: Concepts first, then labs, then a quiz on the domain. Add what you got wrong to your flashcards.

steps.title: Domain 3
steps.description: Concepts first, then labs, then a quiz on the domain. Add what you got wrong to your flashcards.

steps.title: Remaining domains
steps.description: Cover the lighter domains. They are cheaper points per hour than the hard parts of the big ones.

steps.title: One-page summaries and fact flashcards
steps.description: Condense limits, defaults, commands, port numbers and service names into one page per domain and into flashcards.

steps.title: Practice exam 1 and gap analysis
steps.description: Take a full practice exam in exam conditions. For every wrong answer note the objective it belongs to and why you missed it.

steps.title: Fix the weak domains with targeted labs
steps.description: Go back to the objectives where you lost points. Do the lab again without the guide.

steps.title: Practice exams 2 and 3 under real conditions
steps.description: Same time limit, no notes, no pauses. Aim for a clear margin above the passing score.

steps.title: Exam day logistics and last review
steps.description: Check ID, the test centre or online proctoring requirements and the route. Review summaries only and sleep well.

competencies.name: Core concepts
competencies.description: Explain what each service or technology does, when to use it and its trade-offs.

competencies.name: Hands-on skills
competencies.description: Build and configure things from scratch without following a tutorial.

competencies.name: Troubleshooting
competencies.description: Diagnose why something does not work from symptoms, logs and documentation.

competencies.name: Security and best practices
competencies.description: Apply least privilege, encryption, monitoring and cost awareness by default.

competencies.name: Exam technique
competencies.description: Read scenario questions carefully, eliminate wrong options and manage the clock.

cards.front: What is a domain weighting in an exam guide?
cards.back: The percentage of exam questions that come from a domain. Spend your study time roughly in proportion to it.

cards.front: How should you attack a long scenario question?
cards.back: Read the last sentence first to see what is asked, then mark the constraints (cost, security, time, scale) and eliminate options that break them.

cards.front: Why flag a hard question and move on?
cards.back: Minutes spent on one hard question are lost for several easy ones. Flag it, finish the exam, then return with the time left.
Give every user, service or process only the permissions it needs to do its job, and nothing more.
High availability keeps a service running through component failures (redundancy). Disaster recovery restores service after a major outage (backups, failover site).
RTO (recovery time objective): how long you can be down. RPO (recovery point objective): how much data you can lose, measured in time.

cards.front: Encryption at rest vs in transit
cards.back: At rest protects stored data (disks, backups, databases). In transit protects data moving over a network (TLS).
Vertical: give one machine more CPU or memory. Horizontal: add more machines behind a load balancer. Horizontal also improves availability.

cards.front: What is the shared responsibility model?
cards.back: The provider secures the platform itself; you secure what you put on it: data, identities, configuration and access.

cards.front: Why redo a lab without the guide?
cards.back: Following steps proves you can read. Repeating it from memory proves you can do it, which is what scenario questions test.
